trust_decision.summary: With requireWellFormed=true the serializer must refuse to write a DOM element or attribute qualified name into markup unless it matches the XML QName production; the fix puts that decision at the two points where names reach the output buffer: addSerializedAttribute (every attribute name, including synthesized xmlns: declarations) and the ELEMENT_NODE branch before the element name is written.

landing_point.why: The summary says attribute-name injection via setAttribute() bypasses requireWellFormed; every attribute name written by the serializer goes through addSerializedAttribute, so that is the first place a reader looks.

fix_sites.entry_point: XMLSerializer#serializeToString (lib/dom.js:2963), Node#toString (lib/dom.js:2966), NodeList#toString (lib/dom.js:343) — all reach addSerializedAttribute through the shared internal serializeToString

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/dom.js:2966 (Node.prototype.toString) and lib/dom.js:343 (NodeList.prototype.toString) — public wrappers that normalize the same options object and call the shared serializer

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can leave the doctype and wrapper routes alone: the report and the project's @throws list are about element and attribute qualified names (W3C §3.2.1.1), while index.d.ts:1601-1605 frames the implemented §3.2.1.3 doctype checks as publicId/systemId/internalSubset only, and Node#toString / NodeList#toString read as thin aliases of the reported XMLSerializer API rather than separate entry points.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Invalid names must still be serialized verbatim and must not throw when requireWellFormed is off, and the creation APIs setAttribute/createElement must keep accepting any name without throwing (documented divergences). A fix that validates in setAttribute/_createAttribute, or unconditionally inside addSerializedAttribute, breaks that contract and the existing attribute-escaping tests.

O6_input_shapes: prefixed element qualified name whose prefix part is invalid (e.g. 'evil>:child')
unprefixed attribute qualified name written by addSerializedAttribute (e.g. 'a><inject ')
synthesized namespace-declaration name 'xmlns:' + prefix or bare 'xmlns', including a prefix mutated after createElementNS (el.prefix = 'evil>')
attribute node serialized directly as the root node (ATTRIBUTE_NODE branch, name from n.name)
control shapes that must keep serializing without throwing: valid QName, valid prefix, valid attribute name

O7_producer.where: lib/dom.js:2581 (Element#setAttribute, which reaches Document#_createAttribute at lib/dom.js:2444; element names likewise set by Document#createElement at lib/dom.js:2313, and prefix/name are plain writable properties, lib/dom.js:2772)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: DocumentType name is written verbatim into the DOCTYPE declaration even under requireWellFormed; the section validates only publicId, systemId and internalSubset
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory is about element and attribute names, and the project documents its §3.2.1.3 doctype checks as publicId/systemId/internalSubset (index.d.ts:1601-1605), so the doctype name reads as a different check the project never claimed
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~155 lines below the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: EntityReference nodeName is emitted as &name; with no requireWellFormed validation at all
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: createEntityReference already rejects invalid names at creation against the XML Name production (lib/dom.js:2471), so the nodeName is treated as trusted state
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, ~185 lines below the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A nodeFilter may return a string that is pushed into the output raw, bypassing the name checks entirely
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a nodeFilter's returned string is caller-supplied markup by design — an explicit trust boundary, not serializer output
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, above the element branch

O8b_injection_room.where: lib/grammar.js:246 (QName_exact, compiled with the 'm' flag at lib/grammar.js:82)
O8b_injection_room.sibling: any further name check built on the shared QName_exact — a doctype-name check, or a check in another serializer branch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every existing name check reuses this one regex (lib/dom.js:133, lib/dom.js:926, lib/dom.js:2436); because it is multiline-anchored, a name containing a line terminator ('a\n><inject') still matches, so a maintainer reusing it reproduces the same hole the published fix has

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a requireWellFormed check on DocumentType#name next to the existing publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the project adds requireWellFormed checks node type by node type in this switch (lib/dom.js:3259-3269), so the doctype-name check is exactly the next line a maintainer would write

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a prefixed element name synthesized from a namespace table entry instead of from the node's own name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the serializer already composes prefixedNodeName out of namespace bookkeeping, and elements also keep their own _nsMap (lib/dom.js:1739), so a sibling feeding that synthesis from another table is a natural next commit

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second public serialization entry (NodeList#toString) with its own option normalization rather than going through the shared sink
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: NodeList#toString duplicates nodeSerializeToString's option handling, so an entry added later can easily be written against the duplicated logic

O9_family: XML markup injection through unvalidated element/attribute names (CWE-91), requireWellFormed well-formedness enforcement

O10_build.project_tests: test/dom/serializer.test.js — describe('{ requireWellFormed }') at line 304 (CDATASection/Document/Text/Comment/ProcessingInstruction/DocumentType), Node.toString requireWellFormed at line 584, NodeList.toString requireWellFormed at line 614; lib/grammar.js QName_exact is covered by test/grammar/name.test.js

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: validate the name inside Element#setAttribute / Document#_createAttribute (creation time) and only on the attribute path, which throws early and breaks the documented lenient default while leaving element names and the wrapper entry points unfixed
